subsystems.name: Neural interface array
subsystems.role: records and stimulates neurons with high spatial and temporal resolution.

subsystems.name: Neural decoding engine
subsystems.role: converts recorded firing patterns into a digital representation of a sensory experience.

subsystems.name: Neural encoding engine
subsystems.role: converts a digital representation into stimulation patterns that recreate the experience.

subsystems.name: Sensory mapping and calibration system
subsystems.role: learns the correspondence between stimulation patterns and subjective sensations for each individual.

subsystems.name: Data pipeline
subsystems.role: stores, compresses and streams the large volumes of neural data.

subsystems.name: Closed-loop control
subsystems.role: adjusts stimulation in real time based on the user's reported or measured response.

buildSteps.title: Map the neural code for a sensory modality
buildSteps.detail: Using animal models and human volunteers with implanted electrodes, correlate specific patterns of neural activity with specific sensations, such as a particular touch or image.

buildSteps.title: Build a high-channel-count bidirectional interface
buildSteps.detail: Develop arrays that can both record from and stimulate thousands of neurons independently, with long-term stability in the brain.

buildSteps.title: Develop decoding algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Train machine-learning models to translate recorded neural activity into a digital code that captures the essential features of the experience.

buildSteps.title: Develop encoding algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Create stimulation patterns that, when applied to the same neural population, evoke the desired sensation. This requires an inverse model of the neural code.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into a real-time system
buildSteps.detail: Combine recording, decoding, encoding and stimulation into a closed-loop device that can operate with minimal delay.

buildSteps.title: Test in animals
buildSteps.detail: Verify that a recorded experience from one animal can be decoded and re-encoded into another, or that a simple sensation can be replayed.

buildSteps.title: Conduct human trials for simple sensations
buildSteps.detail: Start with basic tactile or visual percepts in volunteers with existing implants, then move to more complex experiences.

buildSteps.title: Scale to rich, multimodal experiences
buildSteps.detail: Expand the number of neurons and modalities to encompass complex memories, emotions or full sensory scenes.

prerequisites.why: arrays with hundreds of electrodes exist, but thousands are needed for complex experiences.
deep brain stimulation and cochlear implants show it works, but spatial and temporal precision is coarse.
visual and tactile codes are partly understood, but higher-level experiences are not.
implants degrade and scar tissue forms, limiting stable recordings to months or a few years.
can handle the data rates, but power and heat constraints in the brain remain.

pathway.milestone: Sensory restoration devices like cochlear implants and retinal prostheses
pathway.unlocks: proof that electrical stimulation can create meaningful percepts.

pathway.milestone: Bidirectional brain-computer interfaces that provide tactile feedback for prosthetic limbs
pathway.unlocks: real-time recording and stimulation in humans.

pathway.milestone: Replay of simple sensory experiences between individuals
pathway.unlocks: demonstration of the core concept in limited settings.
new forms of communication, art and empathy, if ethical and technical barriers are overcome.
